objective: Collect every row-major strict-inequality coordinate without mutating matched-shape grids.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Nested traversal and strict inequality remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Comparing grid-shaped data is a practical diagnostic.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Ragged shape, equality policy and coordinate ownership transfer.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Matching row shapes and constant-cost comparison define a focused task.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: NaN/reference checks prevent modest false matches.

defects: Original checks could not distinguish Object.is or structural JSON comparison from strict inequality.
Mutation after computing differences passed all old fixtures.
Frozen ragged grids and separate output coordinates were unspecified.
rationale: Keep the original !== contract and explicitly state NaN, signed-zero and object-reference behavior. Add matching ragged shapes, frozen rows, preserved inputs and distinct coordinate identities. All revealed variants already satisfy those policies. The O(n²) target names maximum dimension; the text separately explains that actual work visits rows and cells once, avoiding a claim of quadratic work in total cell count.

objective: Check an exact UTF-16-unit subsequence with consistent indexed traversal.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: String indexing and length remain UTF-16 based.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Subsequence checking is mainly an algorithm lesson rather than a complete search product.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Unit consistency, order and single-use positions transfer.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The explicit indexing-unit model fits the existing two-pointer starter/skeleton.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: A revealed-answer Unicode disagreement could otherwise teach and grade inconsistent behavior.

defects: Senior iterated code points in long but indexed UTF-16 units in short, failing emoji matches.
The character unit and normalization/case policy were not stated.
Code-point-only or case-folded alternatives passed old ASCII-only fixtures.
rationale: Preserve the existing reference/junior indexed-unit model and explain UTF-16 units explicitly rather than silently redefining characters. Change senior to indexed traversal too. Against new public fixtures the old reference/junior passed 11/11 while old senior passed 9/11. Tests include emoji, a surrogate-half query, nonadjacent surrogate units, exact case, normalization distinction and multiplicity/order. An independent forward indexOf search over individual units agrees; early/compound traversal estimates stay unknown without a penalty.

objective: Produce a fresh stable descending order of fixed-width date records without cloning posts.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Stable sort and toSorted remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Newest-first date feeds are common application behavior.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Date-format assumptions, stable ties and shallow ownership transfer.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Ten-character valid dates avoid unrelated parsing/time-zone work.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Explicit formats and identity checks avoid silent chronological or data-reference errors.

defects: The original date text examples did not fully define width, validity or time/offset exclusions.
JSON-cloned posts, empty-input reuse and deduplication passed old shape-only cases.
A complexity model for implementation-dependent sorting was absent.
rationale: Specify valid fixed-width Gregorian dates with four-digit years and no time parsing. Preserve original post/nested identities and repeated references in frozen inputs, require a fresh empty result and test leap-day ordering. Reference/junior lexical comparisons and senior localeCompare agree within this fixed ASCII date format. The O(n log n) target explicitly assumes a comparison-sort implementation meeting that bound, rather than claiming ECMAScript guarantees every engine's time complexity. A decorated stable alternative passes.
